title: Deriving the Addition Formulas for sin(A + B) and cos(A + B) from cos(A - B)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: (a) Apply the difference formula for \cos(A - B) to the cofunction identity \sin\theta = \cos(\pi/2 - \theta) to derive the addition formula for \sin(A + B). (b) Derive the addition formula for \cos(A + B) by substituting -B for B in the formula for \cos(A - B).
finalAnswer: \text{(a) } \sin(A + B) = \sin A \cos B + \cos A \sin B, \quad \text{(b) } \cos(A + B) = \cos A \cos B - \sin A \sin B

steps.title: Part (a): Rewrite sin(A + B) Using the Cofunction Identity
steps.explanation: Substitute theta = A + B into sin(theta) = cos(pi/2 - theta) and regroup the argument as the difference of (pi/2 - A) and B.
steps.why: Associativity of real addition allows pi/2 - (A + B) to be grouped as (pi/2 - A) - B.

steps.title: Part (a): Expand Using cos(U - V) and Apply Cofunction Identities
steps.mathExpression: = \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - A\right)\cos B + \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - A\right)\sin B = \sin A \cos B + \cos A \sin B
steps.explanation: Apply the cosine difference formula with U = pi/2 - A and V = B, then use cos(pi/2 - A) = sin A and sin(pi/2 - A) = cos A.
steps.why: Complementary angles pi/2 - A and A satisfy cos(pi/2 - A) = sin A and sin(pi/2 - A) = cos A.

steps.title: Part (b): Substitute -B for B in cos(A - B)
steps.mathExpression: \cos(A + B) = \cos(A - (-B)) = \cos A \cos(-B) + \sin A \sin(-B) = \cos A \cos B - \sin A \sin B
steps.explanation: Write A + B as A - (-B), expand using cos(A - B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B, and simplify using cos(-B) = cos B and sin(-B) = -sin B.
steps.why: Evenness of cosine and oddness of sine convert +sin A sin(-B) into -sin A sin B.
